Code change in `_normalise_private_key`, apple_siwa_service.py:
- `if not text.isascii(): raise ValueError("unparseable private key")` now runs right after the strip, before the PEM check and before any decoding.
- The base64 branch sets `unparseable = True` inside `except (binascii.Error, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError)`.
- `raise ValueError("unparseable private key")` now sits OUTSIDE the except, at `if unparseable:`. The second site, `if not decoded.startswith(_PEM_PREFIX)`, is unchanged and also outside any except.
- No raised ValueError carries a `__context__` or `__cause__`, and the message is always the constant.

New rows: R3 gains four params, `bom-pem`, `smart-quoted-pem`, `zwsp-pem` and `base64-of-labelled-pem`.

- Each param must raise ValueError from both `build_client_secret` and `_normalise_private_key`.
- `_assert_no_key_text_in_exception` runs over the whole chain.

deviations: S3d is killed by a recording b64decode spy, not by the chain helper. Once FC1(b) holds (every raise is outside the except), removing the isascii guard no longer leaks: b64decode's ValueError is caught and a clean ValueError is raised outside. So the R3 non-ASCII params also assert that `_B64Spy.calls == 0` (non-ASCII input is never decoded), with the labelled form as a 2-call control. This is an assertion added beyond the ruling's helper, to make S3d killable.

S3e is killed by a new `_assert_clean_value_error` check (type, constant args, `__context__` None, `__cause__` None) on R3[garbage] and the new params. The chain helper alone cannot see S3e, because binascii.Error's message carries no key text. R3[garbage] was therefore amended. It is red at the previous bytes on that `__context__` assertion, which is the exact defect FC1(b) removes.

`_assert_no_key_text_in_exception` now reports through `pytest.fail` instead of `assert`, with the same condition. pytest's assertion rewriting would have echoed the matched key text into logs. This does not weaken the row.
